I've been working this land for thirty years. My sons are in the city now, and my daughter-in-law helps when she can, but mostly it's me and my older sister-in-law managing the farm day to day. We can't let 7.5 mu sit idle — we need the wheat for our own flour and to sell at the township market, and the maize we sell to the grain station. That's how we've always done it.

The whole field rotates — wheat goes in October after the autumn rains settle, maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June. Same land, two crops a year. That's what everyone in our village does, and it works.

For wheat, I'll go to the village cooperative and get the seed they're pushing this year — probably a Jimai variety, something with decent disease resistance. I plough in autumn before planting, the way my mother-in-law taught me. I'll put down compound fertilizer as base, then top up with urea at jointing. I water four times: before freeze-up, at jointing, at heading, and at grain fill if it looks dry. I'll spray once for weeds in winter, and twice in spring for aphids and rust — those always come.

For maize, I plant right after wheat comes off in June. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the co-op has — that one reliably gives me good ears. Summer rains help so I don't irrigate as much, maybe twice — once if it's a dry July, once before tasseling. Rotary till between crops because there's no time to plough properly. I spray herbicide after planting and then again for corn borer in August.

I'm not changing much from last year. What worked before will work again.
